newsitem.title: USA: IMF official sees no problems with dlr's level now.
newsitem.headline: IMF official sees no problems with dlr's level now.

text.p: An International Monetary Fund official said on Wednesday he had no problems with the current level of the dollar.

"We have no particular difficulties or concerns about the level of the U.S. dollar at this point in time," Flemming Larsen, Deputy Director of the IMF's Research Department, told Reuters Financial Television.
"We have no particular concerns about foreign exchange misalignments," he said, agreeing that the orderly reversal of the dollar sought by major nations seems complete.

Larsen acknowledged that an appreciation of the dollar would "undoubtedly" help European countries, but only a little. He argued that there were much more fundamental reasons for Europe's disappointing economic performance.
"The problems in Europe are not fundamentally due to exchange rates," he said.

He did say though that an early rise of the yen would not be desirable. That is one reason why the IMF is advocating that the Bank of Japan pursue a cautious policy in raising interest rates as the economic recovery there gathers steam.
Tokyo should instead focus on tightening its fiscal stance.
